conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the sequence and which lessons the DQB questions will be answered in
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the DQB questions will be answered across Lessons 2–6 and that the next 'six lessons' are driven by the wonders. Lesson 4 calls itself part of an 'eight-lesson sequence', Lesson 6 refers to its 'four prior lessons' (it is actually the sixth, so five precede it) and Lesson 8 closes the DQB for Lessons 1–7, so the sequence continues through Lesson 8.

Lessons 2, 3, 7 and 8 attribute the patches to fungal mould from airborne spores only. Lesson 5 says the patches are 'fungi and bacteria spread by airborne spores and contact' and that bacterial cells also colonised the food.

conflicts.fact: Effect of refrigeration/cool temperature on mould growth and what it prevents
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says covering the food 'dramatically reduced' colonisation while refrigeration only slows growth. Lesson 7 says covered plus cool equals 'no growth' and that covering 'may not completely stop' mould. Lesson 7 also says drying and salting reduce 'water availability and temperature', though drying and salting do not lower temperature.

conflicts.fact: Number of containers and the pre-incubated sample setup in Lesson 7
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says eight sample containers are set up across six conditions, but labels only A–F (six) containers plus Pre-A and Pre-C. The overview says three food substrates with six container conditions. Lesson 8 refers generally to pre-incubated samples from Lesson 7.

conflicts.fact: Cause of patch variation in colour
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says white, green and black patches reflect different mould species (Rhizopus, Penicillium, Aspergillus). Lesson 2 compares Rhizopus, E. coli and influenza and classifies all patches as fungal moulds without differentiating species. This is compatible rather than contradictory.
